title: (No AI) Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
author: Andrew Liszewski
content:
![Two iPhones running the Apple Health AI Usage Study app.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/applestudy1b.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with [OpenEvidence](https://www.openevidence.com/), a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like _The New England Journal of Medicine_. Participants will use a new iOS app to ask medical questions and then rate the responses based on criteria including accuracy, detail, and relevance.

The app is now available for download, and enrollment starts today, …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1033355/apples-new-study-looks-to-improve-the-effectiveness-of-ai-health-tools)

title: (No AI) Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Nvidia_Jensen_huang_03.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The [latest edition](https://www.theverge.com/column/1033943/jensen-huang-nvidia-china-spying-scandal-resignation) of our [Stepback newsletter](https://www.theverge.com/newsletters) should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning. That includes rumors that Jensen Huang might be trying to find a path back to CEO, and a [statement from Megaspeed](https://www.reuters.com/business/megaspeed-says-alice-huang-left-company-august-2025-2026-11-15/) claiming that Alice Huang hasn't worked for the company since August of 2025, which raises more questions than it answers.

*   Some big names, including [Elon Musk](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1033869/of-course-elon-musk-wants-jensen-huang-to-get-his-job-back) and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, have publicly thrown their support behind a public letter demanding Nvidia "[bring Jensen back](https://standwithjensen.com/)."
